column1: # Query -> the unit that answers it, against a trekr checkout — part of the
# first Rust SEARCH ground truth (the Rust sets originally measured only the
# token_hash tier; a field trial then found Rust search weak, with
# sentence-named test functions dominating).
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Behaviour verified by
# reading the bodies. Same bands as the Ruby sets.
# TEST-TRAP rows: the answer is production code, but the query's vocabulary
# deliberately matches this repo's sentence-named tests (trekr is the corpus
# the field trial tripped on). These are the regression net for
# search::NON_APP_DISCOUNT — if the discount regresses, a test function
# outranks the labeled answer here first.
# Shares "receiver" with the answer's name; the contrast row for the traps.
infer the receiver of a ruby call
# --- no token shared with the answer's identifier ----------------------------
# TEST-TRAP: resolve/mod.rs's own tests are named
# a_bare_call_in_a_class_body_dispatches_on_the_class,
# new_on_a_constant_receiver_resolves_to_class, ... — this wording is theirs,
# the answer is the production resolver they exercise.
where does a bare call inside a class body dispatch
# TEST-TRAP: refs.rs's test is named reads_both_of_rubys_method_notations;
# the production parser is what it exercises.
read both ruby method notations for naming a method
